newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azerbaijan to sign gold deal with U.S. firms.
newsitem.headline: Azerbaijan to sign gold deal with U.S. firms.

text.p: Azerbaijan will sign a contract on Wednesday with a consortium of U.S. companies on a joint deal to mine gold and silver in the former Soviet republic, the presidential press service said on Tuesday.
A statement said the consortium was called RV Investment Group Services LLS. It did not mention what individual companies were involved.
President Haydar Aliyev will sign for the Azeri side.

Prime Minister Artur Rasizade last week said that the draft of the contract called for joint exploration and exploitation of nine gold mines with estimated reserves of 270 tonnes of gold and 2,500 tonnes of silver.
Rasizade said the deal was worth $500 million but it was not clear whether that was the amount to be invested in the project or the value of eventual output.
He said the consortium's share in the deal would probably be 49 percent and the government would hold 51 percent.
The mining sites are located in Azerbaijan's Nakhichevan autonomous republic and the Zangelan, Kelbadjar, Tauz and Kedabek regions of the country.
Kelbadjar and Zangelan have been occupied by forces from neighbouring Armenia since 1993. The two countries are involved in a protracted territorial conflict.
It was not clear how the mines could be utilised while they were under Armenian occupation.
One of the mines, Zod, is situated along the border between Armenia and Azerbaijan.
Armenia signed a contract with Global Gold Corporation of the U.S. on joint exploration of Zod earlier this year. Azerbaijan has protested.
